1. List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Anil Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajendra Prasad Singh,
learned State Law Officer and perused the record.
3.
As informed by learned State Law Officer, notice to the informant has been served on 07.12.2024 but none is present on behalf of the informant even in the revised call.

4. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 254 of 2023, under Sections 363, 506, 366, 376(3) I.P.C.
and Section 5(J)(2), 5L, 6 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Khanpur, District Bulandshahr, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to have enticed away the minor daughter of the informant aged about 13 years between 28.09.20263 to 30.09.2023.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT :
6. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
7. The FIR is delayed by more than four days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
8. The applicant is not named in the FIR.

The name of the applicant has come up later on in the statement of the victim recorded under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
9.

The victim is a consenting party as is but evident from her statement recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C. but she has made her statement in a different way at the stage of her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C.
10.
Out of the said corporeal relationship with the applicant, the victim has given birth to a baby boy.
11. The instant case is just a misuse of process of law.
12. The victim by her looks seems to be major.
13. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.

The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
14.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 30.05.2024.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE :

15. The bail application has been opposed on the ground that as per school certificate of Class-VIth,
age of the victim is less than 16 years.
16. In rebuttal, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the said certificate is not admissible in the light of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

sentences.text: In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785, this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

18. In the case of P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525, the Supreme Court has observed that in the absence of records relating to the birth of the victim, no other documents except the Matriculation or equivalent certificate from the concerned examination board or certificate by a corporation, municipal authority or a Panchayat can be relied upon to ascertain the age of the victim.
19.

entities.text: P. Yuvaprakash vs State Rep. by Inspector of Police, AIR 2023 SC 3525
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

20. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
21.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
22.
Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
23. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

24. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

25. Let the applicant-Pankaj involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Pankaj vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 February, 2025

(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
26. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

27. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
